# How this book was made {.unnumbered}

*Health in Medicine: Nutrition* is authored by the Department of Biochemistry & Nutrition/Metabolism
Systems-based Workgroup, NUS Medicine, with AI assistance.

## The technical build

The book is a static website, built from plain-text source so that every change between versions can
be compared and reviewed. The build has four elements:

- Quarto turns the chapter source (Markdown with embedded citations and cross-references) into this
  linked, searchable website. KaTeX renders the equations, and a BibTeX bibliography is the single
  source of truth for references.
- The interactive parts (the self-assessment quizzes, the branching clinical cases, and the bespoke
  diagrams) are Svelte components, bundled with Vite and hydrated into each page as self-contained
  "islands". Your progress is saved locally in your browser; there is no account and no login.
- A GitHub Actions pipeline rebuilds and deploys the site automatically on every change, so the
  published version always matches the latest source.
- Figures are either original diagrams made for this book or openly licensed images, each credited
  to its source.

## The simulated patient

The live patient conversations in the cases of the
[*Everyday and preventive counselling*](cases-counselling.qmd) and
[*Recognising risk and knowing when to refer*](cases-referral.qmd) chapters run on a separate,
self-hosted language model. The model, an open-weights model from the Qwen family, is served on NUS
infrastructure through an OpenAI-compatible interface. Your messages pass to a small server-side proxy
that holds the access key and applies the safety guardrails. The replies stream back in real time,
each tagged with a mood that drives the patient's expression, and a short rubric grades the encounter
afterwards.

The simulated patient is a practice tool, guardrailed and tested against adversarial probing, and never
a substitute for a real patient or for medical advice. If the model is unavailable, the case says so
and continues.

## The authoring process

The manuscript was drafted with Anthropic's Claude models, run through Claude Code, an agentic
command-line assistant, under close human direction. Rather than one-shot generation, the work used a
deliberately adversarial, multi-agent process built to catch the failure modes these models are known
for. The process had four stages:

1. For each topic, a fan-out of research agents first assembled a source-backed dossier. A separate
   "refuter" agent then re-checked every citation independently, because language models are prone to
   attaching a real claim to the wrong reference. Nothing advanced to drafting until its sources
   survived that check.
2. Each chapter was drafted against a fixed template and style guide: pathophysiology built on earlier
   chapters by name, a Singapore-first framing, and a "recognise the levers and refer" altitude for the
   disease chapters.
3. Separate agents then reviewed each draft adversarially along independent dimensions (clinical
   accuracy against the dossier, house style, the quiz and case design, and the figures), and the
   findings were triaged and fixed.
4. Before anything was committed, deterministic checks rendered the whole book, confirmed that no
   asset or citation was missing, checked the case files for errors, and opened the interactive pages
   in a real browser to confirm they worked.

Medical educators then reviewed and edited the resulting draft.

## A note to the reader

This book is an educational resource, not clinical guidance. Medicine and its evidence change over
time; check against current local guidelines before acting on anything here.
